title: How I learned to stop worrying and love the gamification of finance
summary:
Gamification has a bad name in finance, and rightfully so.
In good gamification, the worst case is small, known, and capped before you start.
The entry fee plus the exit fee, about 5% round trip, and less in practice because the floor rises while you hold.

title: Students who use AI generally score worse at school
summary:
Students who use AI to help them study tend to perform worse at school than those who don’t, according to data from a global OECD educational report.
Students who said they used AI weekly to generally help them learn outperformed nonusers, though not by much.
This likely reflects better access to hardware, stable internet access, and paid AI tools.
AI use also varied widely internationally: Over 95 percent of Vietnamese students reported using AI tools, compared to just 60 percent in Japan.
AI users do have one thing going for them: The study found that curiosity levels correlate with AI use, peaking with daily users.

title: Stoke Space raises $1bn for a rocket that has never flown
summary:

title: Why VCs Are Questioning AI Companies' Big Revenue Claims
summary:

OpenAI has described subscription sales as ARR while calling its newer advertising business an annualized revenue run rate.

title: Microsoft breaks another patch Tuesday record
summary:
Sources tell me that Microsoft will set another patch Tuesday record today, the third in just a few months.
Microsoft typically patches around 100 flaws every month, but in June it set a new record of around 200 fixes.
July’s patch Tuesday was even bigger, with Microsoft patching at least 570 security holes, almost triple the number of June’s record-breaking release.
Microsoft engineers had a chance to catch their breath a bit in August when they plugged nearly 400 security vulnerabilities.
I understand today’s September patch Tuesday is about to set a new record, with more than 650 security fixes for Windows alone.

title: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
summary:
OpenAI announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Tuesday and is adding a new way to tell ChatGPT what you want it to make an image of: by drawing a doodle.
With a new feature called Sketch, you can just draw something right inside ChatGPT and then tell ChatGPT how you want it to make an image based on that sketch.
You can activate the Sketch feature by typing @Sketch into your chat box, and a window will pop up where you can make your drawing.
Here’s my original doodle and the first image ChatGPT made of the cat, which had green eyes.
Screenshot by Jay Peters / The VergeAs for ChatGPT Images 2.5, OpenAI says that it makes images with “more natural lighting and richer textures,” is better at following your editing instructions “across multiple turns,” and that image generation latency has been reduced by “up to 50% compared with Images 2.0.” ChatGPT Images 2.5 is out now for ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users on desktop, mobile, and web, according to OpenAI.

title: It’s GNU Radio Companion, But In The Browser
summary:

Loading it up gives you a very familiar window if you’re used to GNU Radio Companion, and it comes with a set of example flowgraphs that cover a large range of applications.
